newsitem.title: USA: Group vows to fight for Jewish assets across Europe.
newsitem.headline: Group vows to fight for Jewish assets across Europe.

text.p: A Jewish leader battling the Swiss over the return of Holocaust victims' assets vowed on Wednesday to lead similiar fights against other nations of Western Europe including France, Belgium, Holland and Sweden.

In a speech to U.S. Jewish leaders, World Jewish Congress President Edgar Bronfman said: "This is not just about money. It is about Jewish dignity, Jewish rights, Jewish feelings, about being Jewish, about the fact that we are not going to be pushed around any more."
Bronfman, who is also the head of the Seagrams liquor empire, is trying to get the Swiss to return assets in dormant accounts that were deposited by Holocaust victims.

His campaign has led to a search of the archives in which many documents embarrassing to the Swiss have surfaced, including ones showing that Switzerland turned over heirless Polish assets in Swiss banks to Poland so that Swiss citizens could be compensated for the nationalisation of their property in the then Communist country.
Bronfman said that next month Norway will pay an estimated $80 million in compensation for the seizure of property from 800 Jews who died in the Holocaust.

He said that he would now take the fight for restitution to the other countries of Western Europe, naming Belgium, Holland and France, "where the French government gave up Jews before the Nazis even asked for them."
"We will (also) investigate what happened in Sweden," he added.

Bronfman released a previously secret U.S. army document from 1945 found in the National Archives that said allied soldiers found bags of gold fillings from human teeth hidden in a salt mine by the Nazis in western Germany at the end of the Second World War.

The document said the bags of gold fillings were among stacks of gold bars, gold coins, silver, Passover candlesticks, paintings and other assets looted by the Nazis and then hidden in a salt mine in Merkers in western Germany.
Testimony at the Nuremberg War Crimes Tribunal said the Nazis extracted gold from the teeth of people they executed in death camps and melted it down to sell for their war effort.

Bronfman said he released the document to show that the looted Nazi gold his organisation was trying to trace was not just gold bullion taken from the treasuries of Europe, but items from human beings.
He called negotiations with the Swiss over the return of dormant assets very difficult and said, "they are fighting us every inch of the way."

The Swiss Bankers Association and the World Jewish Congress have formed a joint committee to investigate dormant accounts in Swiss banks and Bronfman said they have fought over whether to hire local auditors or an international accounting firm.

New York Republican Senator Alfonse D'Amato, the chairman of the Senate Banking committee and a Bronfman ally in the fight with the Swiss banks, told the meeting that his investigators have found evidence that Switzerland struck an assets return agreememnt with Hungary similiar to the one it had with Poland.
